newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian government, union reach full strike deal.
newsitem.headline: Colombian government, union reach full strike deal.

text.p: Colombia's labour leaders and government ministers reached a deal early Tuesday to end a public sector strike, now in its eighth day.

The accord gives a maximum pay hike of 20 percent for state workers, compared to the government's initial offer of a weighted 13.5 percent. Union heads and government officials also agreed to set up joint commissions to tackle the issue of a series of planned privatizations on a sector-by-sector basis.
Wilson Borja, head of the main public sector workers' union FENALTRASE said the strike would be lifted immediately and that the deal would signed on Tuesday afternoon.

Finance Minister Jos Antonio Ocampo said the salary agreement would cost the government an additional 115 billion pesos but he was confident of slicing 1.3 trillion pesos off the 1997 budget in an effort to rein in the fiscal deficit.

Hernando Hernandez, head of the main oil workers union USO said the deal for public sector workers opened the way for the restart of talks with the state oil company Ecopetrol over a new collective contract but he did not rule out a fresh strike by oil workers if their list of more than 50 demands were not met.

The government and union representatives issued conflicting reports on the full impact of the state workers' strike. President Ernesto Samper said just 10 percent of state workers took part while labor leaders said they succeeded in severely disrupting telecommunications, education, all but emergency health care and even private sector road freight services.
